target_customer: High-throughput screening groups at pharma and biotech drug discovery teams that need to profile many proteins across large sample sets
problem: Profiling hundreds of proteins per sample with legacy immunoassays (ELISA, bead-based multiplex) is slow and costly, so protein data lags far behind DNA sequencing in scale.
business_model: Fee-for-service protein profiling on its nELISA platform through early access programs, later instrument and assay products (Omni 1000 launched May 2025)

founders.name: Milad Dagher
education: McGill University (bioengineering, per BetaKit; degree not stated)
founders.background_notes: BetaKit says the company was founded by bioengineers at McGill and names Dagher as co-founder and CEO.

founders.name: Jeff Munzar
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page. No background found in opened sources.

competitors.name: Olink Proteomics
competitors.what: Proximity extension assay panels for multiplex protein measurement; launched Explore 1536 on an NGS readout in June 2020
competitors.traction_then: Established proteomics vendor with analysis service labs in Uppsala and Boston

technical_complexity.rationale: nELISA combines DNA-programmed antibody pairs with sequencing readout to multiplex sandwich immunoassays at high throughput, which needed novel assay chemistry and lab automation, later published in Nature Methods per press.

defensibility.rationale: Novel assay chemistry and published method, plus reagent and lab operations know-how, are hard to copy. Customers could still switch to Olink or SomaLogic.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it by the sources seen. Nomic stayed independent and raised a Series B in September 2024.

market_need_then: Pharma discovery groups wanted larger protein panels at lower cost; the company said it offered 100s of proteins at 10x throughput and cost advantage versus existing solutions, with pharma pilots in 2021 cited by the CEO.

branding.domain_note: Uses nomic.bio (a .bio domain, not an exact .com) per the company site.

identity.voice_and_tone: Accessible, plain claims such as The $50 Proteome and Accessible. Adaptable. Absolute.

branding.brand_signature: The nELISA product name and The $50 Proteome positioning

brand_strength.rationale: Little press about the brand itself found; coverage is about funding and science. A niche B2B science audience limits brand reach.

outcome_analysis: Nomic stayed independent and active. It rebranded from Nplex Biosciences, raised a $17M Series A in December 2021 led by Lux Capital after pharma pilots, and a $42M Series B in September 2024, then launched Omni 1000 in May 2025. A novel assay technology and repeat backing from Lux, SR One and Real Ventures explain its progress, while the deep science and long sales cycles slowed commercial scale.
notes: Series A release says total funding exceeded 21M, so about 4M of earlier funding (seed or YC era) is not itemized. Series B lead is inconsistent: press release says an unnamed US life-sciences investor, one aggregator says Lux. Total after Series B reported as over 60M by the company, 56M to 59M by aggregators. SomaLogic was a competitor but no source dated at or near the batch was found. Founding year varies by source (2017 per YC and BetaKit).
